questions.k230_mlir_closure: Can generated Contract parameters flow through linalg and Transform Dialect lowering into the same OpenBLAS packing and sgemm_kernel adapter on K230?
questions.model_relevance: What fraction of a real Qwen2.5-0.5B Transformer projection trace is represented by the frozen workload pool?
questions.weighted_boundary: What is the trace-weighted latency and tuning-cost boundary on the local x86 host and, once available, the external targets?

local_x86.workloads: the eight exact GEMM shapes emitted by the Qwen trace
local_x86.measurement_scope: single-thread kernel execution; no model framework, tokenization, attention, or lm_head time

local_x86_measurement_qualification.purpose: diagnose measurement fitness only; qualification timings are excluded from performance claims

acceptance.selection_rule: select the lowest-numbered CPU among qualifying CPUs; never select by throughput

decision.if_pass: freeze the selected CPU and execute confirmatory protocol v2
decision.if_fail: stop local WSL performance claims and retain only correctness, liveness, trace, and static-closure evidence

acceptance.correctness: all rows pass deterministic projection checking
acceptance.path: all generated LLVM IR files call their Transform-selected adapter symbol
acceptance.runtime: all MLIR entry points reach the shared adapter and OpenBLAS sgemm_kernel
acceptance.parity: the workload-cluster interval for C-adapter/MLIR-adapter includes 1.0 or its point estimate differs by no more than 5 percent

qwen_trace.execution: Hugging Face Qwen2ForCausalLM shape execution with parameterized modules replaced by stateless shape-preserving modules
qwen_trace.scope: 24 Transformer blocks; lm_head is retained in the raw trace but excluded from the core projection coverage claim

claim_boundary: The experiment validates a representative MLIR-to-K230 adapter closure and a real model-code GEMM shape trace. It does not claim full-model execution, multithreaded speedup, or universal RISC-V backend portability.
